The spec rejects only 'a date that is not a real YYYY-MM-DD' (3.3), 3.18 sets each APR process's `asOf` to 'the latest permit or application date of the process', and every 6, 12 month and `all` window of that process ends there. Resolution (a narrow fix inside existing tasks, no new field, no schema change): 3.3's `parseApplication` and `parsePermit` take `today` (an ISO date, the day of the fetch, passed from `now` in 3.19) and return `{ error }` for a date after it, so the row goes to quarantine as `parse_error` (3.19 already does this for an `error` row) and never reaches `asOf`. Known cost: a permit whose permit date is rejected counts as still waiting, not issued, until upstream corrects it; the `rejected` count in 3.19's result shows how many. Not changed here: places keep their own `asOf`, so one ranking can compare medians over windows that end in different months (the ranking table does not show each row's window). Making them share one `asOf` per kind needs the report year (the `YEAR` field is parsed but not stored) or a reviewed date in the data, and showing `windowEnd` in the ranking needs a field on `Headline` (session-owned contract); both are for Edan to choose, and anchoring a shared `asOf` to the maximum date in the import is wrong for the reason above.

spikes.fact: What is the exact legal citation for California's 3-calendar-day expedited CalFresh rule (Welfare and Institutions Code 18912, 18914, a CDSS regulation or an ACL letter), is its text on an allowlisted ca.gov or leginfo page, and does CDSS's column `Timeliness Expedited Services Percentage` measure the 3-day or the federal 7-day standard?
spikes.answer: (a) Citation: Welfare and Institutions Code section 18914, as amended by AB 1359 (Chapter 468, Statutes of 2012), effective January 1, 2013. ACL 12-74 (December 24, 2012) states: "applicants determined to be entitled to ES will continue to receive CalFresh benefits no later than the third calendar day following the date the application was filed. For purposes of this section, a weekend (Saturday and Sunday) shall be considered one calendar day. However, if the third calendar day is a nonworking day or holiday, the County Welfare Department (CWD) shall make benefits available on or before the working day immediately proceeing the nonworking day." ACL 12-74 cites 7 CFR 273.2(i) and MPP 63-301.51 and related sections. I did not verify the text of W&I 18912 itself. (b) leginfo.legislature.ca.gov section 18914 returned HTTP 403 to my fetch, so I could not read the statute text from leginfo. ACL 12-74 is on cdss.ca.gov, a ca.gov domain, and I read it. (c) The DFA 296X form (7/13), "CalFresh Expedited Service Quarterly Statistical Report", defines ES as: "California's standard for ES is three calendar days due to provision of the Welfare Rights League v. McMahon settlement; federal standard for ES is seven days, per 7 CFR 273.2(i)(3)(i)." Its Item 4a1 counts benefits issued in 1-3 days and Item 4a2 counts 4-7 days. I did not find a CDSS column titled exactly "Timeliness Expedited Services Percentage" in the CDSS dashboard or its data files, so I cannot say which standard that column measures. The CDSS data dashboard is published as yearly .xlsx files, which I did not open. Not settled: the exact column definition.
spikes.source: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl/2012/12-74.pdf (ACL 12-74, read via WebFetch and pdftotext); https://www.cdss.ca.gov/research/res/pdf/blankforms/DFA296Xv7_13.pdf (DFA 296X 7/13, read via WebFetch and pdftotext). Attempted https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=18914 (HTTP 403). Column not located; no source for it.

spikes.fact: Supabase free plan: the per-object upload limit (believed 50 MB), whether a twice-weekly scheduled import counts as activity that prevents the 7-day pause, the 500 MB database limit including indexes for about 244,000 APR permits, and any statement or transaction time limit on the session pooler that one 660,000-row import transaction could exceed.

spikes.fact: Do the licences and terms of data.ca.gov (HCD APR), data.chhs.ca.gov (DHCS), cdss.ca.gov, DataSF and Keenable permit saving and republishing derived figures and storing fetched pages, and what attribution do they require?
spikes.answer:
Only partly settled. Retrieved 2026-11-15.

- cdss.ca.gov: Settled in part. The Conditions of Use say information is "considered in the public domain, unless otherwise indicated" and "may be distributed or copied as permitted by law." Copyrighted material (e.g., photographs) and information owned by others need the owner's permission. The page does not address saving fetched pages or republishing derived figures specifically. No attribution requirement is stated.
- DataSF: Settled in part. Data is made available under the Public Domain Dedication and License v1.0. Derivative works are covered (Section VII.B), but the page does not say whether derived figures may be republished. Re-identification is prohibited, and combining data to re-identify is prohibited. Individual datasets may carry additional terms. No attribution requirement is stated. Note the source is an sf.gov page for DataSF; the datasf.org URL redirected to sf.gov.
- data.chhs.ca.gov (CalHHS/DHCS portal): Not settled. The disclosure page only links to its Terms of Use at https://data.chhs.ca.gov/pages/terms, which returned HTTP 403. Per-dataset licence metadata varies; some DHCS datasets show "other-license-specified" or no licence.
- data.ca.gov (HCD APR): Not settled. The Terms page https://data.ca.gov/pages/terms-of-use returned 404, and https://data.ca.gov/pages/conditions-of-use also returned 404. The CA Open Data Handbook (https://handbook.data.ca.gov/disclosures) says open licences should have no restrictions on copying, publishing, distributing or adapting, and states no general attribution requirement. Portal-wide terms are unverified; licence is set per dataset.
- Keenable: Not settled. The terms page https://keenable.ai/page/terms-of-use returned 404. A search snippet indicates a Section 6.4 "Data Usage and Attribution Rights" and a Section 6.2 on prohibited activities that mentions bulk data extraction. The caching, republishing and attribution terms were not read.
